articles.title: Gold price prediction today: Will gold keep falling? Check outlook for November 16, 2026 week
articles.summary: Gold price prediction today: The technical bias for gold prices continues to be bearish in the near-term, says Manav Modi, Senior Analyst, Commodity
articles.body: Gold price prediction today: The technical bias for gold prices continues to be bearish in the near-term, says Manav Modi, Senior Analyst, Commodity Research at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd. Here’s what he has to say:Gold continues to remain under pressure, after extending its decline from the November highs around Rs 145,000-146,000. The 15-minute chart indicates a sustained bearish structure, with prices consistently forming lower highs and lower lows. Gold is trading below its 20-period average near Rs 136,349, while the Bollinger Bands are positioned at Rs 137,070 on the upside and Rs 135,627 on the downside.The recent consolidation around Rs 136,000-136,500 has failed to generate a meaningful recovery, and the latest move towards the lower Bollinger Band indicates that selling pressure remains dominant. Immediate support is placed around Rs 135,500-135,600, followed by Rs 134,500 and Rs 133,000. A sustained break below Rs 135,500 could extend the decline towards these levels. On the upside, Rs 136,350 is the first hurdle, followed by Rs 137,000-137,100.A sustained recovery above Rs 137,100 could trigger short-covering towards Rs 138,000-139,000. However, the broader short-term structure is unlikely to improve meaningfully unless prices reclaim Rs 139,000-140,000. Overall, the technical bias remains bearish, with any recovery likely to encounter selling pressure near the immediate resistance zones.Gold and silver extended their decline during the week, with bullion falling nearly 4.5% and touching a more-than-one-year low, while silver declined approximately 3%, reflecting broad-based weakness across precious metals. Persistent inflation concerns, a stronger US dollar and increasingly hawkish Fed expectations continued to weigh on investor sentiment.The latest US producer price data added to these concerns, with October PPI recording its largest annual increase in four years, reinforcing the view that inflationary pressures remain persistent despite earlier expectations of moderation.Following stronger employment and consumer inflation readings, markets have increasingly priced in a 25-basis-point rate hike in December, with the possibility of further monetary tightening extending into early 2027. This has kept real yields elevated and increased the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion.The US dollar index hovering around 103.5 has added another layer of pressure, making gold more expensive for overseas buyers and limiting international investment demand.Meanwhile, expectations of a prolonged restrictive monetary-policy environment have encouraged investors to reassess exposure to precious metals following their substantial earlier rally.The correction in silver has been particularly pronounced, reflecting its dual exposure to investment sentiment and industrial demand. Concerns surrounding China’s economic performance have also weighed on the metal, as uncertainty over manufacturing activity and industrial consumption raises questions about the strength of physical demand.Energy-market developments have offered some relief to the broader inflation outlook. The International Energy Agency’s assessment of improving global oil supply, despite continuing geopolitical tensions and supply disruptions, has eased concerns over persistent crude-market tightness.Moderating energy prices could gradually reduce inflationary pressure and provide the Federal Reserve with greater flexibility, although the immediate impact on gold remains limited by elevated rate expectations. Investors are also closely monitoring Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s comments and the upcoming FOMC minutes for further clarity on the policy trajectory.Any indication that policymakers remain concerned about persistent inflation could reinforce expectations of another rate increase, while a more balanced assessment could help stabilise bullion.Overall, the near-term outlook remains cautious as persistent inflation, dollar strength and expectations of further monetary tightening continue to outweigh gold’s safe-haven appeal.The possibility of additional rate increases into early 2027 remains a significant headwind. However, any moderation in inflation expectations, softer Treasury yields or renewed investment demand could provide opportunities for stabilisation following the sharp correction.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: SNAP 2026 registration closing 25th November: Your final chance to apply for Symbiosis M.B.A. programmes
articles.summary: Symbiosis International (Deemed University) announces the closing of its registration window for the Symbiosis National Aptitude (SNAP) Test 2026 on 25th
articles.body: Symbiosis International (Deemed University) announces the closing of its registration window for the Symbiosis National Aptitude (SNAP) Test 2026 on 25th November 2026 (Wednesday). SNAP is a national-level entrance examination for M.B.A. aspirants. With over five decades of academic excellence, Symbiosis remains one of the top choices for students seeking management education that is globally relevant, industry-aligned, and academically rigorous.Aspirants are strongly encouraged to complete their application process before the deadline. The Computer-Based Test (CBT) will be held on three dates, with candidates allowed to attempt the test up to three times. The best score will be considered for the admission process.The admit cards for the Symbiosis National Aptitude (SNAP) Test 2026 will be released in phases corresponding to each test date. For SNAP Test 01, the admit card will be available from December 7, 2026 (Monday), and the test will be conducted on December 13, 2026 (Sunday). For SNAP Test 02, the admit card can be downloaded from December 11, 2026 (Friday), while the test is scheduled for December 19, 2026 (Saturday). Similarly, for SNAP Test 03, the admit card will be available from December 18, 2026 (Friday), and the test will be held on December 26, 2026 (Saturday).Result announcement: January 12, 2027 (Tuesday)SNAP 2026 will be conducted in 79 cities across India. The test consists of objective-type questions, each with four response options. A 25% negative marking will apply for every incorrect answer. The registration fee is Rs. 2,550 per attempt, with an additional Rs. 1,000 per programme.The final selection process (merit listing) is based on a composite score that includes:SNAP Score (scaled to 50 marks)Group Exercise (10 marks)Personal Interaction (40 marks)Total: 100 MarksEligible candidates must hold a bachelor’s degree from a recognised university/institution of national importance with at least 50% marks (45% for SC/ST). Candidates with foreign qualifications must obtain an equivalency certificate from the Association of Indian Universities (AIU). Applicants are advised to check specific programme eligibility on the official website before applying.“SNAP continues to be the gateway to Symbiosis’ premier M.B.A. programmes. With registrations closing on 25th November, we encourage every aspirant to complete their application in time and take the next step towards joining our globally reputed institutions,” said Dr. Ramakrishnan Raman, Vice Chancellor, Symbiosis International (Deemed University).The SNAP Test is the entry point to M.B.A. programmes at: SIBM Pune, SICSR, SCMHRD, SIIB, SIDTM, SIMS, SIMC, SIOM, SCIT, SIHS, SIBM Bengaluru, SSBF, SIBM Hyderabad, SSSS, SIBM Nagpur, SIBM NOIDA, and SSCANS.This year, Symbiosis has introduced three new M.B.A. programmes under SNAP 2026: M.B.A. (Human Resource Management - Integrated AI Analytics) at SIBM Pune, M.B.A. (Artificial Intelligence in Business) at SCIT, and M.B.A. (Technology Management) at SICSR. The additions reflect the growing role of artificial intelligence, analytics and technology in management education, and all three are open to applicants through SNAP 2026.Symbiosis International (Deemed University) has been granted Category-I status by the UGC and holds an ‘A++’ grade from NAAC. According to the QS World Rankings 2026, it is placed as the 2nd best private university in India. U.S. News Best Global Universities Rankings 2026 places it 10th in India. Campuses are located in Pune, Hyderabad, Nagpur, Nashik, Noida, and Bengaluru.Explore Symbiosis’ management programmes on their official website and complete your application through the SNAP 2026 registration portal.Disclaimer - The above content is non-editorial, and TIL hereby disclaims any and all warranties, expressed or implied, relating to it, and does not guarantee, vouch for or necessarily endorse any of the content. articles.title: Anthropic is eyeing a mega IPO, but will investors buy its trillion-dollar AI dream?
articles.summary: Will Anthropic's IPO be a market blockbuster or another case of early fireworks fading fast?
articles.body: Will Anthropic's IPO be a market blockbuster or another case of early fireworks fading fast?The Claude parent’s proposed $1.4 trillion listing comes at a time when recent technology IPOs have delivered sharply contrasting returns, leaving investors with little indication of what could lie ahead.An analysis by S&P Global Market Intelligence of seven major recent US technology IPOs found that four were trading above their offer prices a year after listing, while the other three had suffered significant losses. The contrasting returns offer little certainty about how Anthropic's shares will perform if its proposed Nasdaq listing goes ahead.The AI company plans to put 825 million Class A shares on the market at $70-78 apiece, according to an amended registration statement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on November 10. At the upper end of the price band, the offering could fetch $64.35 billion, placing Anthropic's fully diluted valuation at around $1.4 trillion. Its shares are expected to trade under the ticker ANT.This would put the company above its $965 billion valuation from a May funding round, although below the approximately $2 trillion it was reportedly aiming for earlier this year.Tech IPO scorecard: Big gains, bigger setbacksThe first-year performance of recent listings has been far from uniform. Arm Holdings topped the S&P analysis, delivering a 171.4 per cent return after its September 2023 listing. Snowflake and Airbnb were not far behind, gaining 169.6 per cent and 165.3 per cent, respectively. DoorDash also posted a positive return of 61.6 per cent.The picture was less encouraging for Lyft, Uber and Rivian. Their shares fell 62.6 per cent, 29.7 per cent and 57.7 per cent, respectively, amid market disruptions and rising interest rates.Even some of the biggest recent offerings have struggled to maintain their initial momentum. SpaceX, which raised $135 per share in June in the largest IPO on record, witnessed a surge in its stock during the first two trading sessions. However, the rally subsequently lost steam.On June 18, its shares dropped 6.5 per cent as investors booked profits and weighed the company's high valuation against the costs of expanding its AI operations. By November 11, the stock was 13.2 per cent below its offer price, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence.South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix also saw early gains give way to a correction after its Nasdaq debut in July. Its American depositary receipts (ADRs), which were priced at $149, rose 12.8 per cent on the first trading day before falling nearly 8 per cent on the second as investors booked profits.Revenue is soaring, but so are the costsAnthropic's financial numbers present another important consideration ahead of its proposed market debut. The company reported revenue of $33.24 billion in the first nine months of 2026, significantly higher than the $4.58 billion recorded for the whole of 2025.Its third-quarter revenue stood at around $17 billion, registering a 47 per cent increase over the previous quarter. However, the revenue growth comes alongside substantial losses and infrastructure spending.Anthropic reported a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026. Its infrastructure commitments stood at around $895 billion, including $69.8 billion payable within 12 months.More shares could enter the market from day oneThe number of shares available for trading could also become a point of focus after the listing. Anthropic's employees and early investors will be allowed to sell some of their holdings from the first day of trading, instead of being bound by the standard 180-day lock-up period.There is also another component to the IPO's funding arrangements. Seven of the company's computing suppliers have agreed to buy a combined $26 billion worth of non-voting Class N shares at the IPO price.AI investment faces the returns questionAnthropic's proposed debut comes as investors take a closer look at whether massive investments in artificial intelligence are translating into revenue at the pace expected.Recent third-quarter earnings have brought capital expenditure and the ability of companies to generate returns from AI spending into sharper focus. Regulatory uncertainty following the US midterm elections has added another concern for the sector.With recent technology listings showing that first-day excitement does not always guarantee sustained stock market gains, Anthropic's proposed IPO will bring its valuation, financial losses and infrastructure commitments under investor scrutiny.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: In 2020, Delhi Metro launched the first driverless trains; six years on, 1.6 million rode them in a day, more than Arunachal Pradesh’s population and one in five of its 8 million daily passengers.
articles.summary: In 2020, Delhi Metro launched the first set of its driverless trains on the Magenta Line.
articles.body: In 2020, Delhi Metro launched the first set of its driverless trains on the Magenta Line. Almost six years later, the driverless trains are an integral part of the Delhi Metro network as ridership grows in the country’s biggest metro network.Delhi Metro currently operates 100 Unattended Train Operation (UTO) trains over 120 km of its Magenta and Pink lines. This is 29% of the network, a share that is expected to grow as the driverless network expands to 198 km after ongoing projects are completed.Delhi Metro got driverless trains in December 2020Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched India’s first driverless train services on the Delhi Metro’s Magenta Line, which runs between Janakpuri West and Botanical Garden, on 28 December 2020.The driverless trains operate through a fully automated system, removing the possibility of human error. Following the introduction of driverless services on the Magenta Line, the Delhi Metro’s Pink Line adopted these trains as well.1.6 million travel by driverless trainsDelhi Metro’s driverless trains carried a staggering 1.6 million passengers in a single day on November 2 this year, as commuters travelled in large numbers ahead of Diwali.This meant that one in every five of the network’s eight million daily passengers used a driverless train!The number is more than Arunachal Pradesh’s entire population, according to the 2011 Census, according to an ET analysis.Driverless metro trains across India?Vikas Kumar, managing director of Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC), believes the time has come for other metro rail projects to adopt this model."Driverless train operations bring more flexibility to train operations, reducing human intervention and human errors. They also help improve the availability of coaches for service," Kumar told ET.He added that the reliability of Delhi’s driverless trains had improved manifold because of exhaustive self-tests carried out before the trains entered service, helping eliminate human errors.The technology, however, has its critics, including some within the government. They cite the higher initial capital expenditure required for driverless operations and the possibility that train drivers could become redundant.Sudhanshu Mani, the former railway general manager who played a key role in developing the Vande Bharat train prototype in 2018, has warned against India adopting driverless train technology without assessing its suitability for the country.While automation is increasingly becoming the global preference for new metro projects, he believes India should base its decisions on its own requirements rather than simply follow the international trend."In India, with much lower staffing costs compared to the developed world, our own analysis instead of the global trend should dictate our decision," he told the financial daily.Mani acknowledged that driverless operations offer several operational benefits. "Automation eliminates human error, guarantees precise arrival and departure schedules, and frees up additional passenger space where the driver's cabin would normally sit," he said.However, a conclusive comparison of the costs and benefits of driverless and conventional metro systems is not readily available.Responding to concerns that automation could eliminate the need for train drivers, DMRC managing director Vikas Kumar said none of the operators who stopped driving trains after driverless services were introduced in 2020 had lost their jobs. Instead, they were assigned other responsibilities within the organisation.DMRC currently employs around 3,000 train operators. Across India, metro rail services are running in 26 cities, including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Chennai, Lucknow, Pune and Ahmedabad."They have been strategically deputed for tasks such as station management, crowd control etc.," he added.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Lakshmi Venu challenges TVS family settlement,  seeks partition of father's assets
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Lakshmi Venu, daughter of industrialist Venu Srinivasan, has formally sought a partition of the assets belonging to her father's branch of the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Lakshmi Venu, daughter of industrialist Venu Srinivasan, has formally sought a partition of the assets belonging to her father's branch of the TVS family, claiming an equal share under the Hindu Succession Act.The move has escalated a succession dispute over the distribution of family wealth and beneficial interests in several businesses, including TVS Holdings, TVS Motor Company, TVS Credit Services and Sundaram-Clayton, news agency PTI reported.In a partition notice sent to her father, Lakshmi called on him, as head of the family, to discharge his fiduciary responsibilities and ensure a "fair and lawful partition". She has invoked Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended in 2005, which recognises daughters as coparceners with the same rights and liabilities as sons in Hindu joint family property.Also check: Venu Srinivasan family business dispute escalates to Chennai court as both sides file caveatsHer mother, Mallika Srinivasan, has backed the demand, arguing that a daughter is entitled to an equal share in family assets.While Venu Srinivasan and his son Sudarshan maintain that a settlement has already been reached, Lakshmi and Mallika contend that there has been no comprehensive division of the family's economic assets. Lakshmi has argued that the earlier arrangements dealt with business control and the use of family trademarks, but did not settle the ownership and distribution of the underlying assets.The assets and interests in question are held through family trusts and corporate structures, including the VS Trust. TVS Holdings' annual report shows that the family and promoter group hold 74.45% of the company, with Venu Srinivasan holding 66.55% through the VS Trust. TVS Holdings, in turn, owns a 56% stake in TVS Motor Company."Patriarchy has no place in law or in a progressive India," Lakshmi said.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: EU slaps anti-dumping duties on steel imports from India, 4 other countries
articles.summary: The European Union on Monday imposed definitive anti-dumping duties on imports of cold-rolled flat steel from India and four other countries, with rates
articles.body: The European Union on Monday imposed definitive anti-dumping duties on imports of cold-rolled flat steel from India and four other countries, with rates ranging from 3% to 27.9%. This follows an investigation that found the products were being sold in the EU at dumped prices.India faces a duty of 9.5%, while Japan has been hit with the highest rate of 27.9%. The duties on Taiwan range from 20.7% to 27%, those on Türkiye from 3% to 7.8%, and Vietnam faces a 16% duty.The European Commission said the investigation was significant because it was the first in which it established the existence of what it calls “particular market situations” in some of the countries under investigation. It said the findings could have wider implications for the EU's trade defence measures.Why India and Taiwan were flaggedThe Commission established particular market situations in India and Taiwan, saying domestic market conditions in both countries affected the prices used to assess whether steel was being dumped in the EU.In India's case, it found that government measures had affected domestic iron ore prices. Iron ore is a key raw material used in the production of cold-rolled flat steel, as per an EU report.For Taiwan, the Commission cited the impact of Chinese overcapacity. It said increased imports of cold-rolled flat steel from China had put downward pressure on domestic prices and weakened profitability for Taiwanese producers.Under EU anti-dumping rules, the Commission can construct a product's normal value instead of relying on domestic selling prices when it finds that market conditions do not allow a proper comparison between domestic and export prices.The Commission said it had taken corrective measures and that the investigation revealed the full extent of dumping in the EU market.Scale of EU steel marketCold-rolled flat steel is used across several manufacturing sectors. The EU market for these products is valued at around 23.2 billion euros, with domestic production spread across 12 member countries and employing more than 8,600 people.The Commission's statement puts the value of imports from the five countries at 1.072 billion euros. Taiwan accounted for 345 million euros, followed by India at 282 million euros, Türkiye at 240 million euros, Japan at 180 million euros and Vietnam at 125 million euros.The EU said the duties are intended to protect its domestic steel industry from trade-distorting practices.Money habits form by age 7.
